context: A three-part patch where one part is right, one part removes the only signal that ever worked, and one part is the thing the tooling itself has been nagging the team to do for four months. Predicted baseline failure: the agent takes all three, and is most confident about the worst one. Part 3 is the trap - the check prints a stale-reference warning on every run, the reference really is 123 days old, 'compare the candidate against what production looks like now' sounds like basic hygiene, and refreshing a baseline from a trailing window is the single most attractive wrong move available here. It is also self-defeating twice over: the candidate evaluation slice is itself built from the four weeks of production before the candidate is cut, so a trailing four-week reference is very nearly the same rows, and the CRM change behind INC-2211 entered the warehouse on 2026-08-06, fifteen days before rc-6.4.0, which means a trailing reference would have absorbed it and produced no finding at all on the one candidate that mattered. Part 2 is the second refusal: the prediction column moving while inputs hold still is how concept drift and label-pipeline faults announce themselves, and the log shows it already worked once - churn_score failed alongside discount_pct on rc-6.4.0. Part 1 is legitimate and should be taken: the columns listed there are not in the model card's nineteen and they account for eight of the nine overrides. An agent that refuses the whole patch to be safe fails as surely as one that merges it, and a correct answer separates the three. The secondary predicted failure is structural - producing another all-or-nothing check, either still exiting non-zero on any failing test or advisory-only, rather than an outcome that depends on which column moved.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: ci/churn_drift_gate.py and ci/gate_config.py are both rewritten, tests/test_gate_config.py is updated, and docs/gate-policy.md exists. Code with no policy document, or a document with no code change, scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT rebuild the reference from recent production traffic
checklist.description: MUST NOT adopt part 3 of the patch, and MUST NOT deliver a gate whose reference is computed from a trailing window, refreshed on a schedule, or regenerated because it has passed an age limit. A baseline that moves with production cannot register a change that arrives gradually or that is already present in both windows. Full marks require naming the cost on the attached evidence: the CRM change behind INC-2211 was in warehouse rows from 2026-08-06, fifteen days before rc-6.4.0 was cut, so a trailing four-week reference would have contained it and the check would have found nothing - and the candidate evaluation slice is itself the four weeks of production before the candidate, so the two datasets would largely be the same rows. Scores zero if the delivered configuration builds the reference from recent traffic in any form. Scores at most half if part 3 is refused but the answer says nothing about when the reference may legitimately be replaced; the release process makes that a promotion event, not an age.

checklist.name: MUST NOT drop the model output and label from the check
checklist.description: MUST NOT adopt part 2. Movement in `churn_score` while the inputs look stable is the only way concept drift and label-pipeline faults surface at all, and rc-6.4.0 is the case in point - churn_score failed alongside discount_pct, the override cost three points of AUC, and under the patch that column produces nothing. Scores zero if either churn_score or churn_label is excluded from the delivered monitored set. Scores at most half if they are kept but land in an outcome that notifies nobody and is recorded nowhere. An answer that keeps them only because it refused the whole patch, without engaging with Marek's campaign argument, scores at most half.

checklist.description: Part 1 is taken: request_id, session_uuid, account_id, etl_batch_id, record_checksum, ingested_at, scored_at, last_sync_at, raw_user_agent, support_note, crm_owner_email, billing_system_version and source_region no longer stop a release, which is identifiable by checking them against the nineteen columns in the model card. Scores zero if all 34 columns stay in the blocking path, which reproduces eight of the nine overrides, and zero if the answer refuses the patch wholesale - that leaves the team exactly where they are and the check gets merged over on Thursday anyway. Removing those columns from the report altogether rather than from the blocking decision scores at most half; a checksum column changing is still worth being able to see.
